title: Weyl dimension formula for dominant induced modules
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $S$ be a semisimple simply connected $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]: it is smooth, connected, affine and of finite type, has no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup, and every surjective homomorphism from a semisimple group with finite central kernel is an isomorphism. Solvable means that successive commutator subgroup schemes become trivial; finite central means finite-dimensional coordinate algebra and commuting after every scalar extension. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq S$ and a Borel subgroup $B\supseteq T$ with unipotent radical $U$, with these notions as in [lem-sfb-rho-section-modules]. Use the character lattice $X=X^*(T)$, roots $\Phi$, positive roots $\Phi^+$ in $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$, simple roots $\Delta$, coroots and integer pairing of [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Put $\rho=\tfrac12\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\alpha\in X$ as in [lem-sfb-rho-section-modules]. A rational $S$-module is an $F$-vector space $V$ with coaction $c_V:V\to V\otimes_F F[S]$ satisfying coassociativity and the counit identity. A submodule is a linear subspace stable under this coaction, and simple means nonzero with only zero and itself as submodules. Write $V^U$ for the vectors whose restricted coaction is $v\mapsto v\otimes1$. A finite-dimensional simple module has highest weight $\eta\in X$ if $V^U$ is one-dimensional and $t v=\eta(t)v$ on this line after every commutative $F$-algebra extension. Write $\dim_F$ for ordinary vector-space dimension, an integer rather than its image in $F$. Let $\lambda\in X$ be dominant, meaning $\langle\lambda,\alpha^\vee\rangle\ge0$ for every $\alpha\in\Delta$, and extend it to $\widetilde\lambda:B\to\mathbf G_m$ by the projection $B\to T$ of [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Define the actual left-translation module
$$E_B(-\widetilde\lambda)=\{f\in F[S]: f(gb)=\widetilde\lambda(b)f(g)\text{ after every commutative }F\text{-algebra extension}\},\qquad (s f)(g)=f(s^{-1}g).$$
This module is finite-dimensional and
$$\dim_F E_B(-\widetilde\lambda)=\prod_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\frac{\langle\lambda+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle}{\langle\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle}.$$
The product and fractions are computed in $\mathbf Q$, each denominator is a positive integer, and the formula holds in every characteristic. For $\Phi=\varnothing$ the product is $1$. The convention uses the roots in $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$; it does not assert simplicity of this induced module.

source.place: Part II, 5.10--5.12: Weyl character/dimension formula for induced modules, together with Kempf vanishing; WANTED: this book is not local. Online corroboration read: Williamson, Algebraic representations and constructible sheaves, arXiv:1610.06261v1, sections 1.2--1.3, equation (1.4), pp.4--6, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1610.06261. Our Borel is opposite to his convention; opposition -w_0 preserves the dimension product.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure], $S$ is reductive and $Q=S/B$ is proper of finite type over $F$. Apply [lem-sfb-homogeneous-line-bundle-sections] with $\chi=-\widetilde\lambda$: its inverse-character equation becomes $f(gb)=\widetilde\lambda(b)f(g)$, and its left action is exactly $(sf)(g)=f(s^{-1}g)$. Thus $E_B(-\widetilde\lambda)\simeq H^0(Q,\mathcal L_{-\widetilde\lambda})$ equivariantly, including over all $F$-algebras. The sheaf is coherent. Apply [lem-pc-coherent-hi] to $Q\to\operatorname{Spec}F$: a field is Noetherian, so the indicated $H^0$ is finite over $F$. This proves finite dimensionality without any simplicity assertion.

source.place: Section 22d, pp.479--480, Theorems 22.50--22.51, with signs corrected to the line-bundle definition in 18c and 22.48; Jantzen 2003 II.4.5 and II.5.10--5.12 are WANTED.

proof.text: The weight $\lambda$ is dominant for the roots in $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$, and the line bundle has fibre character $-\widetilde\lambda$. These are precisely the hypotheses and sign of [lem-sfb-dominant-flag-line-kempf-vanishing]. Hence all its positive-degree cohomology vanishes, over the given field in any characteristic.

source.place: Section 22d, pp.479--480, Theorems 22.50--22.51, with signs corrected to the line-bundle definition in 18c and 22.48; Jantzen 2003 II.4.5 and II.5.10--5.12 are WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-flag-line-euler-alternant] to the same $S,T,B,\lambda$. By step 2 its polynomial $q_\lambda$ is the integral formal character of $H^0$ alone and satisfies $q_\lambda A(-\rho)=A(-\lambda-\rho)$. The direct-sum decomposition stated there gives $\epsilon(q_\lambda)=\sum_\eta\dim_F H^0_\eta=\dim_F H^0$. This equality is in $\mathbf Z$, so it retains the dimension in positive characteristic.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-simply-connected-character-lattice], the simple roots are a rational basis of $X\otimes\mathbf Q$, and the simple coroots form a basis of the dual root system. Together with the root datum in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure], this verifies the spanning and perfect-pairing hypotheses of [lem-sfb-weyl-alternant-augmentation]; $\rho\in X$ is one of the stated hypotheses. That lemma makes every $\langle\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle$ a positive integer. Apply it to $q=q_\lambda$, $\sigma=-\rho$ and $\nu=-\lambda-\rho$, using the polynomial identity of step 3 after extension to $\mathbf Q[X]$. Each numerator and denominator has a minus sign, which cancels in its fraction. Consequently $\dim_F E_B(-\widetilde\lambda)=\prod_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\langle\lambda+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle/\langle\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle$. This computation takes place in $\mathbf Q$. For no roots the same lemma gives the empty product $1$, so the argument includes the trivial group. All inputs hold in every characteristic.
